 Kristina Knickerbocker Speaks at Wright State
 By
 Will Diaz 
 Nov 2, 2026 10:00 am 
 Kristina Knickerbocker, David Hogg and Nico Agosta spoke on the upcoming election at the Democratic rally at the Academic Success Center on Oct. 27.
 A Democratic rally was held at the Academic Success Center on Oct. 27. Check-in began at 6:30 p.m. and the event started at 6:45 p.m. Just before the event began, the Wright State Guardian had the chance to talk to Kristina Knickerbocker. 
 Kristina Knickerbocker is the Democratic candidate in the U.S. House election to represent Ohio's 10th Congressional District. 
 When asked how she planned to reach voters who have yet to receive information on her campaign, Knickerbocker encouraged voters to visit her website. 
 "They can certainly search our website, but join our newsletter, because they will continue to get campaign updates as well as where they may be able to hear me speak, how they can get engaged, and if they're supportive of the campaign and our priorities," Knickerbocker said. "Which is lowering costs, making sure that we can also have an improved healthcare system, and making sure to end corruption in our political system."
 The event began with the main speaker being introduced, starting with Nico Agosta. Agosta is the Co-Founder of the Political Integrity Project, a project that created the Integrity Index , which is a "political finance database that grades politicians on their financial and political integrity." 
 Agosta encouraged students to vote early, sign up to volunteer for Knickerbocker's campaign and talk to friends about voting. 
 Will Diaz 
 Agosta passed the microphone to David Hogg, Co-Founder and President of Leaders We Deserve and former vice chairman of the Democratic National Committee. 
 Hogg discussed how Knickerbocker helps veterans, particularly his father, a veteran with Parkinson's. The illness caused many arguments between the Hogg family and the VA while trying to pay for his hospital visits. 
 "I believe that our government is prioritizing the interest of people like Elon Musk far more than it's prioritizing the interests of people like my family," Hogg said, followed with an endorsement of Knickerbocker. 
 "...I know when she goes to Congress, she's going to be looking out for people like my father, not guys like Elon Musk," Hogg said. 
 Will Diaz 
 Hogg passed the microphone to Knickerbocker. Immediately, Knickerbocker spoke on how she worried for her patients, as a nurse practitioner, about the Big Beautiful Bill. 
 "I called Senator Husted's office. And I called to warn them that the bill that they were going to sign, as it was, was going to kill my patients. I got no response," Knickerbocker said. The next day, the bill was signed into law. 
 Knickerbocker encouraged voters that she would help her "veteran family, military family, my patients in this community."
 During the exclusive interview with Knickerbocker, when asked about the specific actions she intends to take to lower costs, she responded. 
 Knickerbocker intends to lower costs by fighting to end the war in Iran, stating that the U.S. is currently $40 trillion in debt, which has risen since President Donald Trump's first term, when it was $20 trillion. Knickerbocker also intends to "make sure that the Department of Defense actually passes its first audit," as the DOD has "never passed an audit in the history of its existence."
